questions.q: The SI unit of force is
questions.e: Force = mass × acceleration, with unit kg·m/s² = newton. Joule is energy, pascal is pressure and watt is power.

questions.q: The dimensional formula of velocity is
questions.e: Velocity is length per unit time. [LT⁻²] is acceleration and [MLT⁻¹] is momentum.

questions.q: A potential difference of 12 V across a resistor drives a current of 4 A. The resistance is
Three resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 5 Ω are connected in series. Their equivalent resistance is
questions.e: In series the resistances add: 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 Ω.

questions.q: Two 6 Ω resistors are connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance is
questions.e: For two equal resistors in parallel, R(eq) = R/2 = 3 Ω.

questions.q: The majority charge carriers in a p-type semiconductor are
questions.e: Doping with trivalent atoms creates holes, which are the majority carriers in p-type material.

questions.q: A light emitting diode (LED) emits light when it is
questions.e: Under forward bias, electrons and holes recombine at the junction and release energy as photons.

questions.q: In vacuum, all electromagnetic waves travel at about
questions.e: Radio waves, light and X-rays all travel at the speed of light, c ≈ 3 × 10⁸ m/s. 340 m/s is the speed of sound in air.

questions.q: Which of the following electromagnetic waves has the highest frequency?
questions.e: In order of increasing frequency: radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about doping of semiconductors.
I. Doping silicon with phosphorus gives an n-type semiconductor.
II. Doping silicon with boron gives an n-type semiconductor.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Phosphorus is pentavalent and gives extra electrons (n-type). Boron is trivalent and gives holes, so it makes p-type material.

questions.q: Capacitors of 4 μF and 12 μF are connected in series. The equivalent capacitance is
questions.e: In series 1/C = 1/4 + 1/12 = 1/3, so C = 3 μF. Parallel combination would give 16 μF.

questions.q: A mass of 0.5 kg attached to a spring of force constant 50 N/m executes simple harmonic motion. The time period is approximately
A body starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration of 2 m/s². Its speed after covering 25 m is
Photons of energy 5 eV fall on a metal of work function 2 eV. The stopping potential is
questions.e: Maximum kinetic energy = hν − φ = 5 − 2 = 3 eV, so the stopping potential is 3 V.

questions.q: An LED is made from a semiconductor with band gap 2.0 eV. The approximate wavelength of light emitted is (take hc = 1240 eV·nm)
questions.e: λ = hc/E = 1240/2.0 = 620 nm, which is orange-red light.

questions.q: In a common-emitter transistor, the current gain β is 100 and the base current is 30 μA. The collector current is
An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 20 cm. The image is formed
o: 60 cm in front of the mirror, real
12 cm in front of the mirror, real
questions.e: With u = −30 and f = −20, 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = −1/20 + 1/30 = −1/60. So v = −60 cm: a real image in front of the mirror.

questions.q: A source of frequency 500 Hz moves towards a stationary listener at 34 m/s. If the speed of sound is 340 m/s, the frequency heard is approximately
questions.e: f' = f·v/(v − vs) = 500 × 340/306 ≈ 556 Hz. The pitch rises because the source approaches.

questions.q: A 12 V battery of negligible internal resistance is connected to a 4 Ω resistor in series with a parallel combination of 6 Ω and 12 Ω resistors. The current through the 12 Ω resistor is
questions.e: Parallel part = 4 Ω, so total R = 8 Ω and I = 1.5 A. Voltage across the parallel part = 1.5 × 4 = 6 V, so I = 6/12 = 0.5 A.

questions.q: A 4 kg block at rest is pushed along a rough horizontal floor by a 10 N force for 4 m. The friction force is 2 N. The speed of the block after 4 m is
questions.e: Net work = (10 − 2) × 4 = 32 J, which equals kinetic energy. ½ × 4 × v² = 32 gives v² = 16, so v = 4 m/s.
